text.en: A boy hurries to school expecting a scolding and finds a lesson he will never forget.

The story is set in the days of the Franco-Prussian war, after which the districts of Alsace and Lorraine fell to the Prussians. Franz starts for school very late, fearing a scolding from M. Hamel, but finds the school unusually quiet and the villagers sitting at the back. He learns that this is the last French lesson because an order from Berlin says only German will be taught.
Franz now regrets wasting time and not learning his language well. The story shows how a people's language is part of their identity and how we value things only when we are about to lose them.
Learn the words dread, scolding, oppressors, identity and patriotism. The story is told in the first person by Franz.
